question.value: Whether magnetohydrodynamic disk winds (MHD DWs) predicted by water maser observations at 10–100 au in massive YSOs IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35 can be confirmed and characterized on scales of 100–1000 au using millimeter molecular line tracers.

evidence.quote: The goal of this article is to further test the water maser MHD DW predictions focusing on the YSOs IRAS 21078$+$5211 and G035.02$+$0.35, representative of the two characteristic maser kinematic configurations observed in POETS.

what.value: 22 GHz water maser positions, 3D velocities, and radio continuum maps from the POETS survey

evidence.quote: There are two kinds of prevalent maser kinematic configurations: (1) water maser positions and 3D velocities are collimated and trace a fast rotating jet, as in IRAS 21078$+$5211 (cite: Mos16); and (2) the local standard of rest (LSR) velocity ($V_{\rm LSR}$) gradient of the water masers agrees with that of the underlying rotating disk (observed in ALMA thermal lines) and the proper motions point away from the disk midplane at large angles, as in G011.92$-$0.61 and G035.02$+$0.35 (cite: Mos19b).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: J- and CJ-type shock chemistry models for SO and SO2 production and thermal desorption from dust grains

evidence.quote: On the other hand, the recent calculations by (cite: vGel21), accounting for both warm gas-phase chemistry and thermal desorption from dust grains, show that 10–100 au layers of enhanced SO and SO$_2$ abundance can be produced behind J- and CJ-type shocks

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: C-type shock models for CH3OH sputtering and post-shock warm gas depth

evidence.quote: High abundances of CH$_3$OH are expected in the post-shock layers of C-type shocks for shock velocity $V_{\rm s} \gtrsim$12 km s$^{-1}$ sufficiently high for efficient sputtering of the CH$_3$OH molecules off the icy mantle of dust grains (cite: Burk19; Bai26).
For a pre-shock hydrogen number density, $n_{\rm H}$, of 10$^{5}$–10$^6$ cm$^{-3}$, C-type shocks yield post-shock depths of warm molecular gas of $\approx$500–5000 au (cite: Pin93)

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate, image, and continuum-subtract millimeter interferometric datasets

method.value: For NOEMA (IRAS 21078+5211), calibrate and image in GILDAS (Clic/Mapping) with phase self-calibration on continuum (3 loops: 300, 150, 45 s) and uniform weighting, keeping non-self-calibrated cubes for lines at 0.5 km/s resolution. For ALMA (G035.02+0.35), restore calibration via CASA pipeline, image each SPW manually with TCLEAN (Hogbom, Briggs robust=0.5), and separate continuum and line emission in the image plane using STATCONT.

evidence.quote: Calibration and imaging of the data was conducted within the GILDAS framework with Clic and Mapping.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract spectra and fit LTE synthetic spectra to derive gas physical conditions

method.value: Integrate spectra over the lowest 1.3 mm continuum contour toward both YSOs (and two 0.2'' square outflow apertures in IRAS 21078+5211), identify unblended optically thin lines with MADCUBA SLIM, and fit LTE synthetic spectra using MADCUBA AUTOFIT.

evidence.quote: For both IRAS 21078$+$5211 and G035.02$+$0.35, we derived the spectral emission in the direction of the YSO by integrating the signal over the area inside the lowest 1.3 mm continuum contour

Using the SLIM (Spectral Line Identification and Modeling) tool of MADCUBA, we surveyed the spectra to search for molecular species with a relatively large number of unblended and optically thin lines

To derive the physical parameters of molecular gas, we used the tool AUTOFIT of MADCUBA, which compares the observed spectra with the LTE synthetic spectra, taking into account all transitions and the line opacities.

analysis_steps.goal: Construct Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams and test wind launching and shock models

method.value: Construct PV plots along the disk midplane and at offsets along the disk rotation axis (averaging across one beam perpendicular to the cut), compare velocity profiles to Keplerian rotation, test whether the velocity gradient in IRAS 21078+5211 can be gravitationally bound envelope rotation, and compare chemical stratification with C-, J-, and CJ-type shock models.

evidence.quote: To study the gas kinematics, we constructed position-velocity (PV) plots of the molecular emissions along the YSO disk midplane (marked by the dashed black line in Figs. 1, 2, and 3). Before producing the PV plot, the emission was averaged across a beam in the direction perpendicular to the positional cut.

Across the green strip one observes $V_{\rm LSR}$ changes as large as $\Delta V_{\rm rot}$ $\approx$ 6 km s$^{-1}$ over radial offsets as small as $\Delta R$ $\approx$ 0.2$''$ (see Fig. 1a, lower plot). Using these values in Eq. \[dVRap\] to calculate the derivative ${\rm d }V_{\rm rot} / {\rm d }R$, at the extremes of the green strip where $\left|Z_{\rm gs}\right| \approx$ 0.3$''$, we derive a value for the YSO mass, $M$ $\approx$ 44 $M_{\odot}$.

validation.value: Compared disk-midplane SO PV plots with off-disk PV plots along the rotation axis to confirm that SO emission traces wind kinematics rather than solely disk rotation.

evidence.quote: The contribution of the disk kinematics on the PV plot of SO in Fig. 4 can be evaluated by comparing it with PV plots at positions along the jet axis sufficiently far from the disk midplane (see Fig. 9) such that only the outflow motion can contribute. These off-disk PV plots show velocity profiles consistent with that at the disk midplane, confirming that the SO emission traces mainly the wind kinematics.

As in IRAS 21078$+$5211, also in G035.02$+$0.35 the PV plots of SO across the disk midplane and offset of the disk (see Fig. 10) are fully consistent with each other, which ensures that SO is tracing the rotation profile of the gas in the wind.

findings_qualitative.value: In IRAS 21078+5211, SO, SO2, HC3N, CH3CN, and CH3OH emissions are elongated along the radio jet axis with a transversal V_LSR gradient and radially nested widths (SO2 and HC3N narrowest near the axis, SO intermediate, CH3CN and CH3OH widest in a funnel/ring pattern).

evidence.loc: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS)
evidence.quote: In IRAS 21078$+$5211, the emissions of several molecules, particularly SO, SO$_2$, CH$_3$CN, and CH$_3$OH, are distributed along the axis of the previously identified radio jet, and present a local standard of rest (LSR) velocity ($V_{\rm LSR}$) gradient transversal to the jet axis.

The wind in IRAS 21078$+$5211 harbors many molecules with a clear radial distribution, going from SO$_2$ and HC$_3$N, found close to the jet axis, through SO, covering larger radii, to CH$_3$CN and CH$_3$OH, with the maximum width.

findings_qualitative.value: In G035.02+0.35, CH3CN, CH3OH, HC3N, and SO2 are confined to the rotating disk midplane, whereas SO is the only molecule extending well outside the disk into the wind.

evidence.loc: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS)
evidence.quote: In G035.02$+$0.35, the same molecules are instead distributed along the (sky-projected) major axis of the rotating disk reported previously, and their $V_{\rm LSR}$ gradients consistently trace the disk rotation. The corresponding PV plots present Keplerian profiles. SO is the only molecular species whose emission extends well outside the disk.

findings_qualitative.value: In both YSOs, SO shows a Keplerian-like rotation profile both at the disk midplane and at off-disk positions along the rotation axis, while SO2 is compact and shows the steepest velocity-position profile.

evidence.quote: In both sources, the SO emission is one of the most radially extended and presents the clearest Keplerian-like velocity profile in the PV plots, while SO$_2$ is spatially compact and yields the steepest velocity-position profile.

As in IRAS 21078$+$5211, also in G035.02$+$0.35 the PV plots of SO across the disk midplane and offset of the disk (see Fig. 10) are fully consistent with each other, which ensures that SO is tracing the rotation profile of the gas in the wind.

findings_qualitative.value: SiO 5-4 emission is resolved out at the ~250 au scales of the interferometric observations.

evidence.quote: For completeness, we note that the SiO 5–4 emission, another potential outflow tracer, is resolved out at these small scales.

claims.hypothesis: The protostellar winds in IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35 on 100–1000 au scales are magneto-centrifugally launched rotating winds rather than gravitationally bound rotating envelope gas.
claims.experiment: Mapped molecular line velocity gradients and constructed PV diagrams along the disk midplane and offset along the rotation axis, and calculated the central mass required if the transversal velocity gradient in IRAS 21078+5211 were due to centrifugal equilibrium in the envelope.
claims.result: SO and SO2 show transversal V_LSR gradients and Keplerian-like PV profiles both on and off the disk midplane; explaining the gradient in IRAS 21078+5211 (Delta V_rot ~ 6 km/s over 0.2'' at |Z| ~ 0.3'') via gravitational rotation requires ~44 M_sun, far exceeding the known YSO mass of 5.6 +/- 2 M_sun.
claims.finding: The spatial and velocity distributions of SO and SO2 trace rotating winds magneto-centrifugally launched from the YSO disks.

evidence.quote: Using these values in Eq. \[dVRap\] to calculate the derivative ${\rm d }V_{\rm rot} / {\rm d }R$, at the extremes of the green strip where $\left|Z_{\rm gs}\right| \approx$ 0.3$''$, we derive a value for the YSO mass, $M$ $\approx$ 44 $M_{\odot}$.
Therefore, we can conclude that the observed $V_{\rm LSR}$ gradient is by far too large to correspond to the rotation of the YSO envelope, and has to be linked instead with the rotation of the wind.

In both sources, the SO emission is one of the most radially extended and presents the clearest Keplerian-like velocity profile in the PV plots, while SO$_2$ is spatially compact and yields the steepest velocity-position profile. Our analysis of these kinematic findings supports the case of a wind magneto-centrifugally launched from the YSO disk.

claims.hypothesis: The rotating molecular winds originate from a radially extended MHD disk wind (DW) rather than ambient gas entrained by a compact X-wind.
claims.experiment: Measured the radial spatial distribution and LTE physical conditions (T_ex, N_col) of SO, SO2, HC3N, CH3CN, and CH3OH in both targets using MADCUBA and compared them with C-type and J/CJ-type shock chemistry models.
claims.result: In IRAS 21078+5211, SO2 has higher T_ex (118–168 K) than SO (18–33 K) and decreases in N_col away from the axis while CH3OH and CH3CN form a wider ring/funnel; in G035.02+0.35, only SO extends into the wind while other molecules remain in the hot (257–470 K) disk.
claims.finding: Both the chemical stratification in IRAS 21078+5211 (internal J/CJ shocks for SO2/SO vs. external C-shocks for CH3OH) and the absence of molecules other than SO in the G035.02+0.35 wind (due to shock-ionization dissociation in the disk atmosphere) are explained by a radially extended MHD DW and rule out an entrained X-wind.

evidence.loc: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS)
evidence.quote: The comparison with models of molecule formation and excitation in shocks indicates that the different radial extension of the molecular species observed in the protostellar wind of IRAS 21078$+$5211, as well as the lack of molecules, except SO, in the G035.02$+$0.35’s wind, can be well explained in terms of a radially extended MHD DW, rather than a compact X-wind.

since the excitation temperature of SO$_2$ is found to be systematically higher than that of SO at all the explored positions (see Table 3), in agreement with production in stronger shocks, and the continuous decrease in the SO$_2$ column density from near the YSO through small to large radii (see Table 3) clearly indicates its higher concentration in faster gas closer to the outflow axis.

In G035.02$+$0.35, only SO traces the wind, while the other molecular emissions are confined inside the disk. That already excludes the possibility of a X-wind, i.e., that the wind gas is entrained from the surrounding medium, as we should see other molecules, as well.

claims.hypothesis: SO and SO2 thermal line emissions at 100–1000 au scales trace the same MHD disk wind kinematics identified by 22 GHz water maser VLBI observations at 10–100 au scales in luminous YSOs.
claims.experiment: Compared the orientation, velocity gradients, and rotation profiles of SO and SO2 emission at ~250 au resolution in IRAS 21078+5211 and G035.02+0.35 with POETS VLBI water maser and JVLA radio continuum measurements.
claims.result: The molecular wind kinematics at 100–1000 au match the two maser kinematic regimes observed at 10–100 au (collimated rotating jet in IRAS 21078+5211 and wider disk wind in G035.02+0.35).
claims.finding: SO and SO2 emissions are preferential tracers of MHD DWs at 100–1000 au scales in luminous YSOs and confirm the water maser results at 10–100 au.

evidence.loc: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS)
evidence.quote: This study provides compelling evidence that the SO and SO$_2$ emissions can be used to trace MHD DWs in luminous YSOs at scales of 100–1000 au, and confirms the results derived with water masers at scales of 10–100 au.
The gas kinematics traced by water masers at scales of 10–100 au and determined via thermal molecular lines at scales of 100–1000 au are very consistent.

why_this_data.value: The NOEMA long-baseline dataset for IRAS 21078+5211 and the archival ALMA Cycle 4 Band 6 dataset for G035.02+0.35 overlap in frequency and provide matched linear (~250 au) and velocity (~0.5 km/s) resolutions, enabling a direct comparison of two YSOs of different mass (5.6 vs ~20 M_sun) representing the two POETS water maser kinematic configurations.

evidence.quote: IRAS 21078$+$5211 has been recently reobserved with NOEMA at 1.3 mm using long baselines within the large program CORE (cite: Beu18; Gie21; Ahm23); for G035.02$+$0.35, ALMA Cycle 4 Band 6 archival observations are available. These two interferometric datasets overlap in frequency, and provide comparable linear ($\approx$250 au at the target distance) and velocity ($\approx$0.5 km s$^{-1}$) resolutions, which is optimal for a comparison of the gas kinematics between the two sources.

why_this_method.value: Briggs weighting with robust = 0.5 was chosen as a compromise between angular resolution and sensitivity to extended emission; STATCONT was used to statistically determine continuum levels per pixel; MADCUBA AUTOFIT was used to fit LTE synthetic spectra across multiple optically thin transitions spanning a wide range of excitation energies.

evidence.quote: with the robust parameter set to 0.5 as a compromise between resolution and sensitivity to extended emission.

to determine the continuum level of the spectra and subtract it from the line emission, we used STATCONT (cite: Sanc18), a statistical method of estimating the continuum level at each position of the map from the spectral distribution of the intensity at that position.

We selected the CH$_3$CN, CH$_3$OH, and SO$_2$ molecules (see Table 3) that in both targets have optical depths of less (or much less) than 0.25, and cover a sufficiently wide range in excitation energy to allow for a reliable estimate of the excitation temperature.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gravitationally bound rotation of the ambient YSO envelope as the cause of the transversal V_LSR gradient in IRAS 21078+5211 (rejected because it requires a central mass of ~44 M_sun, far exceeding the measured 5.6 +/- 2 M_sun).

evidence.quote: We can reasonably rule out that the observed $V_{\rm LSR}$ gradient transversal to the jet axis is due to the rotation of the ambient gas induced by the gravitational force of the YSO.
Therefore, we can conclude that the observed $V_{\rm LSR}$ gradient is by far too large to correspond to the rotation of the YSO envelope, and has to be linked instead with the rotation of the wind.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Compact X-wind entraining ambient gas (rejected because it cannot explain the nested radial chemical differentiation in IRAS 21078+5211 or the absence of all observed disk molecules except SO in the wind of G035.02+0.35).

evidence.quote: In G035.02$+$0.35 the protostellar wind is traced by SO emission only. That already rules out the possibility that we are observing ambient gas entrained in a fast wide-angle X-wind as there is no reasonable explanation why all the other observed molecular emissions would not be present in the wind.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photoevaporated disk wind in G035.02+0.35 (rejected because water maser velocities >= 20 km/s exceed typical photoevaporative wind speeds of <= 10 km/s, and radio continuum emission is orders of magnitude below the ZAMS Lyman continuum level).

evidence.quote: The high maser velocities, $\ge$20 km s$^{-1}$, favor a MHD DW rather than a photoevaporated DW, whose typical speeds are $\le$10 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Hol94; Ale14).

limitations_admitted.value: SiO 5-4 emission is resolved out at the small spatial scales sampled by the high-resolution interferometric observations.

evidence.quote: For completeness, we note that the SiO 5–4 emission, another potential outflow tracer, is resolved out at these small scales.

limitations_admitted.value: MADCUBA spectral fits assume a single velocity component per molecular species with negligible density and temperature gradients.

evidence.quote: We warn that a single component was fit for each molecular species, under the assumption of negligible density and temperature gradients.

limitations_admitted.value: In IRAS 21078+5211, SO lines are optically thick (tau_max = 5 to 16), leading to large relative uncertainties in the derived SO column densities.
Angular resolution (~0.1'' or ~250 au) is insufficient to vertically resolve the disk structure in G035.02+0.35, causing molecular gas, dust, and free-free continuum to appear spatially overlapping.

evidence.quote: Figure 3 shows that the emissions of the molecular lines, dust, and free-free continuum are basically overlapping in the disk. That is certainly due to insufficient angular resolution to resolve the disk structure vertically, since ionized and neutral gas cannot be cospatial.

referee_caveats_inferred: In IRAS 21078+5211, only 4 SO transitions and 2 HC3N transitions are covered, and the SO lines have high optical depths (tau_max up to 16), making LTE single-component excitation temperatures and column densities for SO and HC3N poorly constrained.

The Keplerian curves in the PV diagrams (Figs. 4, 5, 9, 10) are illustrative overlays using previously published YSO masses rather than quantitative dynamical fits of MHD disk wind streamlines or launching radii.

The ALMA C40-8 configuration for G035.02+0.35 has a minimum baseline of ~92 m, which filters out extended outflow structure and may affect the apparent lack of extended molecular emission compared to NOEMA (minimum baseline ~58 m).
